text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.66% today as oil prices bounced back after a five-day losing streak, with crude climbing on tentative hopes for diplomatic resolution in the Middle East. Iran signaled willingness to negotiate over the Strait of Hormuz, and Ukraine floated an "energy ceasefire" proposal — both developments that could ease geopolitical supply concerns that had weighed on energy stocks over the past week. The stock had fallen 5.8% over the prior two weeks as those tensions mounted.

The recovery today is modest and partly reflects oil's own rebound rather than company-specific strength. The 18-cent gap between U.S. crude ($96.41) and global prices ($114.89) also hints at tightness in domestic supply — a situation that could support refiner margins if the diesel export ban proposal gains traction, though that remains uncertain.
